edges.description: Internalized elementary bodies establish chlamydial inclusions and convert into replicative reticulate bodies.
Intracellular chlamydial growth and antigen release recruit inflammatory leukocytes that convert infection into visible follicular conjunctivitis.
intermediate_mechanisms: Infected epithelial cells and chlamydial antigens recruit acute inflammatory cells.
Neutrophil- and T-cell-rich inflammation damages the conjunctival mucosa.

edges.description: Conjunctival inflammatory follicles are a key clinical expression of adult inclusion conjunctivitis.
Ocular chlamydial inflammatory pathology manifests as conjunctivitis.
Inflammatory conjunctival vascular injection produces conjunctival redness.
Adult inclusion-conjunctivitis inflammation can include a papillary conjunctival reaction.
Chlamydial conjunctival inflammation produces ocular discharge in adults and bloody discharge in a subset of neonates.
Neonatal chlamydial conjunctivitis can present with inflammatory eyelid swelling.

nodes.description: C. trachomatis replicates within a membrane-bound inclusion by alternating between infectious elementary bodies and replicative reticulate bodies; this expands the infected conjunctival epithelial-cell population.

evidence.reference_title: Differential Effects of Small Molecule Inhibitors on the Intracellular Chlamydia Infection.
evidence.snippet: Chlamydia are obligate intracellular bacteria that reside within a membrane-bound compartment called the chlamydial inclusion inside a eukaryotic host cell.

evidence.reference_title: Impact of nutrients on the function of the chlamydial Rsb partner switching mechanism.
evidence.snippet: Chlamydia undergo a biphasic developmental cycle alternating between the infectious elementary body (EB) and the replicative reticulate body (RB).

nodes.description: Ocular chlamydial infection recruits inflammatory effector cells into the conjunctiva; guinea-pig C. caviae experiments support neutrophils as causal contributors to primary ocular chlamydial pathology, and human cohorts document the resulting subacute or chronic follicular/papillary conjunctivitis.

evidence.reference_title: Essential role for neutrophils in pathogenesis and adaptive immunity in Chlamydia caviae ocular infections.
evidence.snippet: The adaptive response was also altered, with increased C. caviae-specific IgA titers in tears and serum and decreased numbers of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in infected conjunctivae.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics and ompA serovar correlation in adult inclusion conjunctivitis: a cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: Patients presented with subacute or chronic conjunctivitis with variable conjunctival hyperaemia, follicular reaction, papillary hypertrophy and discharge.

nodes.description: Infectious C. trachomatis elementary bodies are deposited onto the conjunctiva and taken up by conjunctival epithelial cells, initiating the intracellular ocular infection.

nodes.description: Chlamydial conjunctivitis requires systemic antibiotic therapy rather than topical-only bacterial-conjunctivitis treatment; oral azithromycin and doxycycline are adult inclusion-conjunctivitis regimens.
